editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a room where the only way to talk to your loved ones is through a computer screen. That is the heartbreaking setup you get here. You follow eleven different people who are totally cut off from the rest of the world. You will see a son who just wants to touch his sick mother's hand and a therapist who is slowly falling apart. It feels very heavy and sad, but there are these small, sweet moments where love grows even when people cannot actually be together. It is a quiet movie that makes you think about how much we take for granted just being in the same room as someone.

The acting is the best part because the actors have to show so much emotion through a screen. The slow speed might bore some people, but it really helps you feel the loneliness of the characters. If you like stories that tug at your heartstrings, you should definitely check this out. Since it is such a visual experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the details. If you prefer to own it, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that while the screens provided a way to talk, they could never replace real human touch. You see the characters finally facing the reality of their loss and isolation. The son eventually gets the closure he needs with his mother. It wraps up by reminding you that love survives even in the worst conditions, but the pain of being apart is a heavy burden that doesn't just disappear.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about family and loss.
